description: Backend: make the message send path resilient so a working local model (Ollama qwen3) never produces a silent no-op. ROOT CAUSE (traced in code): tauri-app send_message_inner builds the provider registry with providers::build_registry(configs.iter(), ...), which calls ProviderRegistry::build_all and short-circuits on the FIRST config-row build failure via `?`. The prior 'clean-empty picker' fix already switched list_available_models_inner/provider_diagnostics_inner to a RESILIENT per-row build (loop over build_from_config, capture per-row build_errors, isolate failures) but send_message_inner was NOT given the same treatment. So if the user has ANY un-buildable provider row alongside the working Ollama row (e.g. a misconfigured cloud/embedded row), send_message REJECTS with an Internal CommandError, the frontend's awaited sendMessage rejection is discarded, and the user sees no assistant reply AND no error: exactly the reported symptom. Fix: build the registry resiliently in send_message_inner exactly as list_available_models_inner does, so a single un-buildable row is isolated and the working Ollama provider still routes and generates. This leaves run_turn's existing MessageError-on-failure path intact for genuine provider/stream errors. This is a Rust-only change; frontend visibility is FEAT-002.
steps: In hybrid-orchestrator/crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs, in send_message_inner, REPLACE the fail-fast `let registry = providers::build_registry(configs.iter(), state.secret_store.as_ref()).map_err(...)?;` with the SAME resilient per-row build used by list_available_models_inner: start from `providers::builtin_registry()`, loop over `&configs` calling `registry.build_from_config(cfg, state.secret_store.as_ref())` and, on Err, skip that row (do not abort the turn). Mirror the existing pattern in list_available_models_inner precisely (including the shared-embedded-instance bridge: `registry.insert_instance(std::sync::Arc::new(providers::EmbeddedProvider::from_shared(state.embedded_engine.clone())));`) so send routing observes the same providers the picker enumerates.

Keep the subsequent `list_models(&registry, &configs, &pricing).await?.models` candidate enumeration as-is (its errors are surfaced by list_available_models's UI, not routing). Ensure imports still compile (builtin_registry / EmbeddedProvider are already referenced elsewhere in the file). Confirm no now-unused import of build_registry remains in send_message_inner (build_registry may still be used by other code; check `providers::build_registry` usages with grep before removing any import).

Add a Rust unit test in the commands.rs #[cfg(test)] module (mirroring send_message_inner_rejects_invalid_input and list_available_models_inner_empty_when_no_providers) named e.g. send_message_inner_tolerates_unbuildable_provider_row: seed a persisted ProviderConfig row whose factory build FAILS (e.g. a row that requires a secret that is absent, or an otherwise un-buildable kind) ALONGSIDE a valid conversation, then assert send_message_inner(&state, &valid_conversation_id, "hello", None) returns Ok(()) (the turn spawns) rather than Err. Use the existing test_state()/test helpers. The turn's actual generation will no-op without a live provider, which is fine; the assertion is that the COMMAND no longer rejects because of one bad row.
Do NOT change run_turn or the CoreEvent enum in this feature.
acceptance_criteria: send_message_inner no longer calls providers::build_registry (fail-fast); it builds the registry per-row and isolates a single un-buildable provider row.
A new commands.rs unit test proves send_message_inner returns Ok even when a persisted provider row fails to build, as long as the conversation id/content are valid.
The change is Rust-only; no CoreEvent shape change; existing tauri-app tests still compile.
cargo clippy -D warnings has no new warnings (no unused imports introduced).
verification: Run `cargo test -p tauri-app` under hybrid-orchestrator/ and confirm the new send_message_inner_tolerates_unbuildable_provider_row test plus existing tests pass (CI/where toolchain+network available).
Run `cargo clippy -p tauri-app -- -D warnings` and confirm clean.
Run `cargo fmt -p tauri-app -- --check` (per-crate) and confirm formatted.
findings: Implemented in hybrid-orchestrator/crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs. Replaced the fail-fast `providers::build_registry(configs.iter(), ...)?` in send_message_inner (around line 1682) with the SAME resilient per-row build list_available_models_inner uses: `let mut registry = providers::builtin_registry();` then `for cfg in &configs { let _ = registry.build_from_config(cfg, state.secret_store.as_ref()); }` (per-row Err is isolated/skipped, not aborted), followed by the shared-embedded bridge `registry.insert_instance(std::sync::Arc::new(providers::EmbeddedProvider::from_shared(state.embedded_engine.clone())));`. The rest of send_message_inner is unchanged: it still calls `list_models(&registry, &configs, &pricing).await?.models`, derives local_provider_ids, and spawns run_turn (which retains its MessageError-on-failure path, untouched). Added unit test `send_message_inner_tolerates_unbuildable_provider_row` in the #[cfg(test)] module: seeds a conversation via seed_conversation(), persists an un-buildable GenericOpenAI row (no base_url, factory rejects it) via ProviderRepo::insert, and asserts send_message_inner(&state, &id, "hello", None).await.is_ok(). The un-buildable-row pattern mirrors the existing provider_diagnostics_inner_reports_unbuildable_row test. IMPORT AUDIT: `providers::build_registry` was always called fully-qualified (never in a `use`), and is now only referenced in comments/docstrings, so no import removal was needed and none is unused. builtin_registry/EmbeddedProvider/insert_instance are already referenced by list_available_models_inner. Chose `let _ = build_from_config(...)` (Result is not #[must_use], so clippy-clean) instead of logging, because `tracing` is NOT a dependency of the tauri-app crate. VERIFICATION: `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml -- --check` PASSES (no diff). `cargo build`/`test`/`clippy` for tauri-app CANNOT run in this INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox: tauri-app is under [workspace] exclude and its external `tauri` dependency is not cached (crates.io returns 403 offline: `error: no matching package named tauri found`). Build/clippy/test are therefore CI/user-build verification. Note: an offline cargo invocation incidentally rewrote hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.lock (dropped a routing entry); reverted it via git checkout so the commit contains only the commands.rs change. Rust-only; no CoreEvent shape change; run_turn/pipeline untouched.
